method: The page implements Dan Morey's color estimate. Each malt contributes malt color units, MCU = (pounds of grain x degrees Lovibond) / gallons of batch volume, and the bill's units are summed before the curve is applied: MCU = sum(lb x degL) / gal. Morey's power fit turns that sum into the predicted color, SRM = 1.4922 x MCU^0.6859, which tracks measured beers well below 50 SRM and flattens above it, where 50 SRM is effectively black. EBC is the same 430 nm absorbance scaled by 25 instead of 12.7, so EBC = SRM x 25 / 12.7 (about 1.97 x SRM); a rating entered in EBC is converted back with 12.7 / 25 before it enters the sum, so a bill can be entered in either scale. Weights are kilograms or pounds (1 lb = 0.45359237 kg) and volume is litres or US gallons (3.785411784 L), all converted to pounds and gallons for the formula; entered values are echoed back in the unit that was used. Limits are 0.5-2,000 L, 0.001-500 kg per grain, 0.5-2,000 degL (1-4,000 EBC) per grain and 12 malts; rows that are left blank are ignored and the page reports MCU, SRM, EBC, total grain weight, and each malt's MCU and share of the color. It predicts measured color, not perceived darkness: wort pH, boil time and vigor, kettle caramelization, fermentation and the beer's own haze all move the real figure, and the fit is an approximation of a spectrophotometric measurement.

sources.title: Goldman, J., Craft Beer & Brewing: Seeing the Color in your Future (MCU = (pounds of grain x degrees Lovibond) / gallons, and Morey's SRM = 1.4922 x MCU^0.6859, which holds below 50 SRM where 50 SRM is effectively black)
Wikipedia: Standard Reference Method (SRM = 12.7 x the 430 nm absorbance through 1 cm of beer, and EBC = 25 x the same absorbance, so EBC = SRM x 25 / 12.7)
